skills.name: dependency-injection
skills.description: Wires dependencies for testable code — composition root, constructor or factory injection, narrow ports, lifetimes, injected time and config, fakes, and DI anti-patterns. Use when writing a service, handler, repository or hook, when logic news up clients or reads env or time, or when a test needs jest.mock.

skills.name: design-patterns
skills.description: Picks a design pattern from a concrete symptom, offering the lighter TypeScript option first — strategy, factory, adapter, decorator, repository, pipeline, result type and more. Use when a pattern is named, when asked which pattern fits, or for repeated switches, cross-cutting concerns or vendor coupling.

skills.name: design-principles
skills.description: Applies SOLID and OOP principles as checks — encapsulation, cohesion, composition over inheritance, YAGNI, functional core — mapped to TypeScript. Use when designing or refactoring classes and modules, choosing class vs function vs union, or asking if code is too coupled or over-engineered.

agents.name: design-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews a diff or a set of files for software design problems — tight coupling, god objects, missing dependency injection, leaking vendor types, and also needless patterns and pass-through layers. Read-only. Use when asked to "review the design", "is this over-engineered", "is this too coupled", or before merging a change that adds classes, layers or abstractions.
